candidates.tagline: Meta designed camera glasses to look exactly like normal sunglasses so no one would judge you. Now everyone judges you.
candidates.story: Meta's Ray-Ban smart glasses were deliberately designed to be indistinguishable from regular sunglasses so people wouldn't feel judged wearing them; that exact design decision enabled users to secretly film strangers without detection, earning the glasses the nickname 'pervert glasses,' and now legitimate wearers are too scared to wear them in public — Instagram cracked down on covertly-shot videos from the glasses on July 28, 2026.
candidates.why_funny: The feature that was supposed to make the glasses socially acceptable — looking completely normal — is the same feature that made them socially radioactive.
candidates.alt: Ray-Ban Meta Gen 1 smart glasses and their white charging case resting on a surface, looking identical to regular Ray-Ban sunglasses with no visible camera or recording indicators

candidates.tagline: A gaming console from 2020 just got a 43% price hike in Europe. In 2026. Because Microsoft needs the RAM for its AI.
candidates.story: Microsoft raised Xbox Series X/S prices by up to €200 (43%) across Europe and £170 in the UK on August 1, 2026 — four years into the console's lifespan — citing memory shortages caused by AI data center demand; the same AI infrastructure Microsoft has been investing billions in is the primary driver of the memory crisis, making Xbox gamers in Europe effectively subsidize Microsoft's AI ambitions.
candidates.why_funny: Consumer electronics normally get cheaper as hardware ages; Microsoft has managed to make a six-year-old console more expensive while blaming a shortage their own AI spending helped cause.
candidates.alt: Xbox Series X console on display at an Albert Heijn supermarket in Hillegersberg, Rotterdam, Netherlands, showing the sleek black tower design in a European retail setting
